                             Internet Appendix for
“Cross-Sectional Expected Returns: New Fama-MacBeth
      Regressions in the Era of Machine Learning”
                                    Not for Publication
                                         April 28, 2023



A1. Forecast Construction

This section details the construction of the cross-sectional out-of-sample return forecasts in
the Fama-MacBeth framework described in Section 2 of the paper.


A1.1. Smoothed WLS Forecast

Step 1 Estimate a month-t cross-sectional multiple regression via WLS:

                                       Jt−1
                                       X
                         ri,t = at +          bj,t zi,j,t−1 + εi,t   for i = 1, . . . , nt .     (A.1)
                                       j=1



Step 2 Compute the month-(t + 1) smoothed WLS forecast:

                                               Jt
                                               X
                           S-WLS
                        r̂i,t+1|t = āWLS
                                      t   +             WLS
                                                      b̄j,t zi,j,t   for i = 1, . . . , nt+1 ,   (A.2)
                                                j=1

     where

                                               M −1
                                        1 X WLS

                                        M m=0 t−m

                               WLS      1 X WLS
                             b̄j,t =         b̂                 for j = 1, . . . , Jt ,                (A.4)
                                        M m=0 j,t−m


     M is the size of the window for smoothing the coefficient estimates over time, and âWLS
                                                                                          t

           WLS
     and b̂j,t are the WLS estimates of at and bj,t , respectively, in Equation (A.1). For a
     characteristic to be included in Equation (A.2), it needs to be available in months t − 1
     and t.


A1.2. Smoothed LASSO Forecast

Step 1 Estimate a month-t cross-sectional multiple regression via the weighted LASSO:

                                       Jt−1
                                       X
                         ri,t = at +          bj,t zi,j,t−1 + εi,t      for i = 1, . . . , nt .        (A.5)
                                       j=1

A1.3. Combination LASSO Forecast

Step 1 For each characteristic, estimate a month-(t − 1) cross-sectional univariate regression
     via WLS:


             ri,t−1 = cj,t−1 + dj,t−1 zi,j,t−2 + εi,t−1        for 1, . . . , nt−1 ; j = 1, . . . , Jt−2 .    (A.9)



Step 2 For each characteristic, compute a month-t univariate regression forecast:


                       (j)                 ˆWLS
                     r̂i,t|t−1 = ĉWLS
                                   j,t−1 + dj,t−1 zi,j,t−1      for 1, . . . , nt ; j = 1, . . . , Jt−1 ,    (A.10)


     where ĉWLS       ˆWLS
             j,t−1 and dj,t−1 are the WLS estimates of cj,t−1 and dj,t−1 , respectively, in Equa-

     tion (A.9). For a characteristic to be included in Equation (A.10), it needs to be available
     in months t − 2 and t − 1.

Step 3 Estimate a month-t cross-sectional Granger and Ramanathan (1984) multiple regres-
     sion via the weighted LASSO:

                                          Jt−1
                                          X            (j)
                            ri,t = ξt +          φj,t r̂i,t|t−1 + εi,t   for i = 1, . . . , nt ,             (A.11)
                                          j=1



     where we impose the restrictions that φj,t ≥ 0 for j = 1, . . . , Jt−1 in Equation (A.11). Let
     Jˆt ⊆ {1, . . . , Jt−1 } denote the index set of univariate forecasts selected by the LASSO
     in Equation (A.11).

Step 4 For each characteristic, estimate a month-t cross-sectional univariate regression via
     WLS:


                         ri,t = cj,t + dj,t zi,j,t−1 + εi,t       for 1, . . . , nt ; j = 1, . . . , Jt−1 .     (A.12)

     forecast:

             j,t and dˆj,t
                       WLS
                           are the WLS estimates of cj,t and dj,t , respectively, in Equa-

     available in months t − 1 and t.

                                  C-LASSO       1 X (j)

A1.4. Encompassing LASSO Forecast

Step 1 For each characteristic, estimate a month-(t − 2) cross-sectional univariate regression
     via WLS:


            ri,t−2 = cj,t−2 + dj,t−2 zi,j,t−3 + εi,t−2            for 1, . . . , nt−2 ; j = 1, . . . , Jt−3 .   (A.15)



Step 2 For each characteristic, compute a month-(t − 1) univariate regression forecast:


                   (j)                   ˆWLS
                 r̂i,t−1|t−2 = ĉWLS
                                 j,t−2 + dj,t−2 zi,j,t−2       for 1, . . . , nt−1 ; j = 1, . . . , Jt−2 ,      (A.16)

                                                           4
     where ĉWLS       ˆWLS
             j,t−2 and dj,t−2 are the WLS estimates of cj,t−2 and dj,t−2 , respectively, in Equa-

     tion (A.15). For a characteristic to be included in Equation (A.16), it needs to be
     available in months t − 3 and t − 2.

Step 3 Estimate a month-(t − 1) cross-sectional Granger and Ramanathan (1984) multiple
     regression via the weighted LASSO:

                                       Jt−2
                                       X              (j)

     Let Jˆt−1 ⊆ {1, . . . , Jt−2 } denote the index set of univariate forecasts selected by the
     LASSO in Equation (A.17).

Step 4 For each characteristic, estimate a month-(t − 1) cross-sectional univariate regression
     via WLS:


            ri,t−1 = cj,t−1 + dj,t−1 zi,j,t−2 + εi,t−1          for 1, . . . , nt−1 ; j = 1, . . . , Jt−2 .   (A.18)

     available in months t − 2 and t − 1.

A1.5. Smoothed Random Features Forecast

Step 1 Create the S × J weight matrix Ω, where each element ωs,j is drawn independently
     from N (0, 1/S); also create the S-dimensional vector τ , where each element τs is drawn
     independently from N (0, 1/S).

Step 2 Compute the random features for month t − 1:

                                 Jt−1
                                                        !
                                 X
             gi,s,t−1 = χ τs +          ωs,j zi,j,t−1         for i = 1, . . . , nt ; s = 1, . . . , S,   (A.36)
                                  j=1



     where χ(x) = max{x, 0}.

Step 3 Estimate a month-t cross-sectional multiple regression via weighted ridge regression:

                                         S
                                         X
                         ri,t = κt +           ψs,t gi,s,t−1 + εi,t        for i = 1, . . . , nt ,        (A.37)
                                         s=1


     where the regularization hyperparameter is selected via ten-fold cross validation.

Step 4 Compute the random features for month t:

                                Jt
                                                    !
                                X
              gi,s,t = χ τs +         ωs,j zi,j,t       for i = 1, . . . , nt+1 ; s = 1, . . . , S.       (A.38)
                                j=1



Step 5 Compute the month-(t + 1) smoothed random features forecast:

                                                    S
                                                    X
                        S-RanFeat
                     r̂i,t+1|t    = κ̄Ridge
                                      t     +               Ridge
                                                          ψ̄s,t   gi,s,t    for i = 1, . . . , nt+1 ,     (A.39)
                                                    s=1




                                                          9
     where

                                                      M −1
                                                   1 X Ridge
                                    κ̄Ridge
                                      t     =           κ̂   ,                                                        (A.40)
                                                   M m=0 t−m
                                                      M −1
                                     Ridge         1 X Ridge
                                   ψ̄s,t   =            ψ̂                 for s = 1, . . . , S,                      (A.41)
                                                   M m=0 s,t−m

     M is the size of the window for smoothing the coefficient estimates over time, and
     κ̂Ridge
       t
                   Ridge
             and ψ̂s,t   are the weighted ridge estimates of κt and ψs,t , respectively, in Equa-
     tion (A.37).



A2. Forecast Evaluation

This section derives Equations (37) and (41) in Sections 3.2 and 3.3, respectively, of the paper.

(33) in the paper is given by

Setting the derivative to zero and solving for ζt yields

                                      Pnt                                           

                                          i=1 i,t    ûi,t|t−1    − ûi,t|t−1



Inspection of ζt∗ reveals that it is equivalent to the WLS slope coefficient estimate in a regres-
sion of the demeaned forecast error for A on the difference between the demeaned forecast
errors for A and B. By the Frisch-Waugh-Lovell theorem, ζt∗ is thus identical to the WLS
estimate of θt in Equation (41) in the paper.
